title: Quadratic Equations
seo_title: Quadratic Equations Class 10 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 4)
standard_text: Standard form of a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0); solutions by factorisation and by using the quadratic formula; relationship between discriminant and nature of roots; situational problems based on quadratic equations related to day to day activities (summary of the CBSE syllabus)

key_sub: D = b² − 4ac decides the nature of the roots.
body_html:
How it works

A quadratic equation can be written as ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. Always expand and simplify before deciding.

Solve by factorisation (split the middle term) or by the quadratic formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a).

The discriminant D = b² − 4ac tells the nature of the roots: D > 0 two distinct real roots, D = 0 two equal real roots, D < 0 no real roots.

Example

Solve 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0.

2x² − 2x − 3x + 3 = 0

(x − 1)(2x − 3) = 0

Answer: x = 1 or x = 3/2

Example

Find k so that kx(x − 2) + 6 = 0 has equal roots.

kx² − 2kx + 6 = 0

D = 4k² − 24k = 0

Answer: k = 6

Common mistakes

  • Deciding from the look of an equation without expanding it.
  • Using b² + 4ac for the discriminant.
  • Keeping a negative answer for a length, speed or age.

faq.a: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with b² − 4ac ≥ 0, the roots are x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a).

faq.q: What does the discriminant tell us?
faq.a: D = b² − 4ac. If D > 0 there are two distinct real roots, if D = 0 two equal real roots, and if D < 0 no real roots.

faq.q: How do I solve a quadratic equation by factorisation?
faq.a: Write it as ax² + bx + c = 0, split the middle term into two terms whose product is ac, factorise and set each factor to 0.

faq.q: Why do we reject one root in word problems?
faq.a: A length, speed, age or number of items cannot be negative, so the negative root does not fit the situation.

items.q: What is the nature of the roots of 2x² + 5x − 3 = 0?
items.e: D = b² − 4ac = 49 > 0, so two distinct real roots.

items.q: Find the positive value of k for which 3x² + kx + 75 = 0 has two equal roots.
items.e: D = k² − 4(3)(75) = 0, so k² = 900 and k = ±30. The positive value is k = 30.

items.q: Find k so that x² + 4x + k = 0 has two equal roots.
items.e: Equal roots when D = 0: 4² − 4(1)k = 0, so k = 4.

items.q: What is the nature of the roots of 9x² + 12x + 4 = 0?
items.e: D = b² − 4ac = 0 = 0, so two equal real roots.

items.q: Find k so that x² + 24x + k = 0 has two equal roots.
items.e: Equal roots when D = 0: 24² − 4(1)k = 0, so k = 144.

items.q: Find the positive value of k for which 2x² + kx + 18 = 0 has two equal roots.

items.q: Find k so that 3x² + 24x + k = 0 has two equal roots.

items.q: Two positive numbers add up to 21 and multiply to 104. What is the smaller number?
items.e: Let one number be x, so the other is 21 − x. x(21 − x) = 104 gives x2 − 21x + 104 = 0, so (x − 8)(x − 13) = 0. The smaller number is 8.

items.q: The sides of a right-angled triangle are x cm, (x + 3) cm and (x + 6) cm. Find x.
items.e: x2 + (x + 3)2 = (x + 6)2 gives x2 − 6x − 27 = 0. The roots are 9 and −3; a length is positive, so x = 9.

items.q: Two positive numbers add up to 27 and multiply to 170. What is the smaller number?
items.e: Let one number be x, so the other is 27 − x. x(27 − x) = 170 gives x2 − 27x + 170 = 0, so (x − 10)(x − 17) = 0. The smaller number is 10.

items.q: The product of two consecutive odd positive integers is 1,023. Find the smaller integer.
items.e: Let them be x and x + 2: x(x + 2) = 1,023 gives x² + 2x − 1,023 = 0, so the smaller is 31.

items.q: The product of two consecutive odd positive integers is 2,499. Find the smaller integer.
items.e: Let them be x and x + 2: x(x + 2) = 2,499 gives x² + 2x − 2,499 = 0, so the smaller is 49.

items.q: A rectangular plot is 6 m longer than it is wide. Its area is 55 m². Find its length.
items.e: Width x m, length (x + 6) m: x2 + 6x − 55 = 0, so (x − 5)(x + 11) = 0 and x = 5. The length is 11 m.

items.q: Nisha's brother is 5 years older than her. 3 years ago, the product of their ages was 84. How old is Nisha now?
items.e: Let Nisha be x years old: (x − 3)(x + 2) = 84. The positive root gives 10 years.

items.q: The product of two consecutive odd positive integers is 675. Find the smaller integer.
items.e: Let them be x and x + 2: x(x + 2) = 675 gives x² + 2x − 675 = 0, so the smaller is 25.

items.q: The product of two consecutive odd positive integers is 1,295. Find the smaller integer.
items.e: Let them be x and x + 2: x(x + 2) = 1,295 gives x² + 2x − 1,295 = 0, so the smaller is 35.

items.q: A train travels 240 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 12 km/h more, it would have taken 1 hour less. Find the speed of the train.
items.e: 240/x − 240/(x + 12) = 1 gives x² + 12x − 2,880 = 0. The positive root is 48 km/h.

items.q: The product of two consecutive positive whole numbers is 132. Find the larger number.
items.e: x2 + x − 132 = 0 gives (x − 11)(x + 12) = 0. x = 11 (the positive root), so the larger number is 12.

items.q: When 5 times a positive number is added to its square, the result is 66. Find the number.
items.e: x2 + 5x = 66 gives (x − 6)(x + 11) = 0. The positive answer is 6.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 44 cm and an area of 117 cm². Find the length of its longer side.
items.e: If one side is x, the other is 22 − x. x(22 − x) = 117 gives x2 − 22x + 117 = 0, so the sides are 9 and 13. The longer side is 13 cm.

items.q: A train travels 600 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 10 km/h more, it would have taken 2 hours less. Find the speed of the train.
items.e: 600/x − 600/(x + 10) = 2 gives x² + 10x − 3,000 = 0. The positive root is 50 km/h.

items.q: When 3 times a positive number is added to its square, the result is 270. Find the number.
items.e: x2 + 3x = 270 gives (x − 15)(x + 18) = 0. The positive answer is 15.

items.q: A rectangular plot is 6 m longer than it is wide. Its area is 216 m². Find its length.
items.e: Width x m, length (x + 6) m: x2 + 6x − 216 = 0, so (x − 12)(x + 18) = 0 and x = 12. The length is 18 m.

items.q: The product of two consecutive positive whole numbers is 210. Find the larger number.
items.e: x2 + x − 210 = 0 gives (x − 14)(x + 15) = 0. x = 14 (the positive root), so the larger number is 15.

items.q: The product of two consecutive odd positive integers is 323. Find the smaller integer.
items.e: Let them be x and x + 2: x(x + 2) = 323 gives x² + 2x − 323 = 0, so the smaller is 17.

items.q: The sides of a right-angled triangle are x cm, (x + 17) cm and (x + 18) cm. Find x.
items.e: x2 + (x + 17)2 = (x + 18)2 gives x2 − 2x − 35 = 0. The roots are 7 and −5; a length is positive, so x = 7.

items.q: A rectangular plot is 6 m longer than it is wide. Its area is 91 m². Find its length.
items.e: Width x m, length (x + 6) m: x2 + 6x − 91 = 0, so (x − 7)(x + 13) = 0 and x = 7. The length is 13 m.
